provisions.quote: A licensee shall not disclose nonpublic personal health information about a consumer or customer unless an authorization is obtained from the consumer or customer whose nonpublic personal health information is sought to be disclosed.

Lead that North Dakota has no comprehensive privacy law

consumer_health_data.note: No comprehensive privacy law or consumer health data law found in the Century Code. A 2023 privacy bill, HB 1330, failed in committee per leads. The legislature meets in odd years, so 2025 is the latest session.

crossCheck.note: No comprehensive or consumer health data law found, as the researcher said. The insurance rule 45-14-01-17 (effective 2001-12-01) is an opt-in for one non-HIPAA holder class. It has broad insurance-function exceptions. Adjudicator may weigh scope.
problems: Search missed NDAC chapter 45-14-01, an insurance department rule in force since December 1, 2001.

45-14-01-17 bars insurance licensees from disclosing nonpublic personal health information without the person's authorization. Licensees include life, disability and property insurers and producers that HIPAA does not cover.
Under the D1 anchor, a law covering one class of non-HIPAA holder that requires consent for that class earns level 2.
Search log checked only an AG identity theft page, not the insurance regulator's rules.
